info.title: Tò He Platform API
info.description: Backend for the Tò He hub. Games never call it directly; see docs/contracts.

get.summary: Runtime configuration for the hub.

delete.summary: Remove a provider from the account (needs step-up level 2); never the last way in.

get.summary: A profile's card by its public ID, as this account may find it: never a child of another account.
Allowed avatars and age bands, and how many profiles an account may own.

post.summary: Give this device its key (ADR 0043): a cookie, renewed on use, 90 days. A device that has one keeps it.

get.summary: A proof-of-work to solve before signing up or asking for a password reset, when /api/config says proofOfWork.

post.summary: Start signing up: a code goes to the email. 202 whether or not the address has an account.
The code from the email creates the account and its first profile, which plays at once.
Sign in; sets the session cookie. An only profile without a PIN plays at once.
A code to set a new password goes to the email, if it has an account. 202 either way.
The code sets a new password; every other session ends.
Sign out this device.

get.summary: The device session (account, profiles, active profile, parent gate); 204 when signed out.

post.summary: A code goes to the new email. Needs step-up level 2, or the password with the request.
The code makes the new email the one that signs in; every other session ends.

put.summary: Set or change the manage PIN (needs step-up level 2); opens profile management.
Set or change the password (needs step-up level 2); every other session ends.

post.summary: Accept the terms and privacy notice in the version the hub shows.

delete.summary: Delete the account (needs step-up level 2): it stops now, and goes for good after seven days unless someone signs in to it.

patch.summary: Turn the account's telemetry on or off.

get.summary: The step a sign-in back from a provider waits for, on this browser; 404 when none.

delete.summary: Forget the sign-in waiting on this browser.

post.summary: The provider vouched for no address: a code goes to this one.
The code proves the address: an account with it is linked at once; otherwise sign-up follows.
A code to the account's address, to prove it before the provider is linked.
The code, or the account's password, links the provider to the account and signs in.
A name and the terms finish signing up with the provider; the first profile plays at once.

put.summary: Choose who plays on this device. Locks the parent gate.

post.summary: The manage PIN opens profile management on this device for 10 minutes (step-up level 1).
The password opens account security, and profile management, for 10 minutes (level 2).
A code to the account's email, for stepping up without the password.
The code opens account security, and profile management, for 10 minutes (level 2).
Add a profile to the account (at most five).
Bring a device profile into the account with its id, saves and scores (ADR 0043); 409 id_taken when the id cannot be taken.
Upload a device profile's saves and scores under one of the account's profiles: the newer save wins (ADR 0043).

patch.summary: Edit one of the account's profiles.

delete.summary: Delete one of the account's profiles — never the last one — and everything of it, for good.

post.summary: Make — or bring up to date — a device profile's server copy, with the terms its player accepted; 409 id_taken when the id cannot be taken.

delete.summary: Delete a device profile's server copy and everything of it, for good (ADR 0034); its id is retired. 410 device_profile_moved when it moved to another device.

post.summary: A transfer code for this device's profile, with its saves and scores: six digits and a secret, ten minutes, replacing any before.

get.summary: The profile's live code: open, or asked once a new device typed its six digits; 410 device_profile_moved once it moved.

post.summary: The old device's answer to six typed digits: yes moves the profile now, no ends the code.
Redeem a transfer code on this device: the secret moves the profile at once, six digits ask the old device first.

get.summary: The transfers this device redeemed, newest first, while their answer is kept: a lost answer is read here.
A transfer this device redeemed: asked, done (with the profile, its saves and scores), declined or expired.
This device's profiles that moved to another device with a transfer code.
Games available in the hub, filtered by the active profile's age band.
One game by id (not found if the active profile is too young for it).
Every save of the active profile, for a device to catch up.

put.summary: Store the active profile's save of a game; the last write wins.

post.summary: Record runs of the active profile; the same clientId again raises that run's score.

get.summary: The account's board of a game: each profile's best this week or of all time.
A community's or the server's board of a game: the first 50 and the viewer's place, by trust.

post.summary: Open a ranked run of a game (ADR 0030): its id and the seed to play it from; it closes the last one.
Hand a ranked run's moves and score in; the server replays them with the game's verify module.
Store a batch of technical telemetry from a device (sent by the hub with sendBeacon).

get.summary: Errors, frame times, metrics and counts per game version over the last days (operator token).
Rooms of a game the active profile may see: public ones it may join, and the ones it sits at.

post.summary: Open a room for a game; the active profile hosts it and takes the first seat.

get.summary: Open rooms the active profile sits at, to go back to one.
The active profile's online results in a game, and its account's board of the week.
The active profile's last 20 finished online hands of a game, newest first.
A finished hand the active profile played, with its seed and actions, to replay it in the game.
A room by its 6-digit code (spaces ignored), to preview before joining; rate limited.
A room the active profile sits at, or may see in the lobby.

patch.summary: The host changes the room before a hand: seats, visibility, lock, bots, timer, house rules.

post.summary: Sit at a room: an empty seat, or between hands a bot's.
Watch a table without a seat, if its host allows spectators: only what is public is shown.
Ask a profile to the table — of the account, or another account's as its owner allows (ADR 0033): it shows in their hub for 10 minutes.

get.summary: Tables someone asked the active profile to — by its ID, or from its own account — for the next 10 minutes.

post.summary: Leave the seat; during a hand a bot finishes it. The room closes when the last person leaves.

put.summary: The host seats a bot, or empties a seat (removing a bot or a player).

post.summary: The host starts the first hand; empty seats get bots if the room fills them.

Make a share link to a game, as the acting profile: a `named` feature — a device profile with its terms accepted, a child only with "play with others" on; 30 a day per profile, 60 per device key. An `entry` link carries the game's payload (at most 2 KB), only for a game that takes share entries; its level is raised to the game's.

get.summary: The acting profile's share links, newest first (100 at most), with their state and counts; accounts made only from three upward.

patch.summary: A new expiry for one of the acting profile's links, from now: one hour to 90 days.

post.summary: Revoke one of the acting profile's links: it resolves as revoked from now on.
Resolve a share link by its code to a typed intent — ok, expired, revoked, used_up or unknown; counts it opened. Limited per address (an IPv6 address by its /64).

Resolve a share link to open its game: takes one use and counts it played; an `entry` link answers with its payload and version (ADR 0045). A link asking `named` or `account` needs such a player (403 level_required). Limited as opening.

get.summary: Whether the account has an authenticator for the console (accounts with a platform role).

post.summary: A new authenticator key for the console, while two-factor authentication is off (a platform role and a password, step-up level 2).
A code from the new key turns two-factor authentication on; recovery codes once (a platform role and a password, step-up level 2).
